[[Category:Social psychology]]
The '''observer effect''' refers to the phenomenon that a person's performance on a given task is often influenced by the presence or absence of an audience.<ref>{{#cite:Q3470}}</ref>

== Influencing factors ==

[[Source:Social facilitation: A meta-analysis of 241 studies (Scholarly article)|name-author]] conducted a [[meta-analysis]] on 241 studies and found:

=== Visible non-expert audience ===

In general, the presence of a '''non-expert''' audience '''visible''' to an individual

* '''improves''' the '''speed''' and '''quality''' for performing '''simple tasks''';
* '''worsens''' the '''quality''' when performing '''complex tasks''', especially when the audience is '''unfamiliar'''
* '''worsens''' also the '''speed''' when performing '''complex tasks''' when the audience is '''unfamiliar''', '''no impact''' when the audience is '''familiar'''

=== Invisible non-expert audience ===

In contrast, when the same '''non-expert audience''' is '''invisible''' to the individual (e.g, behind their back), there is

* '''no experimentally significant impact''' on '''speed''' on '''any task''';
* '''similarly negative impact on quality''' when performing '''complex tasks''' to a visible audience;
* an '''uncertain impact''' on '''quality''' when performing '''simple tasks'''.

=== Expert panel ===

In contrast, the presence of a '''panel of domain experts'''

* does '''not''' have an experimentally validated '''effect''' on '''speed''';
* significantly '''increases''' '''physiological arousal''' for '''complex tasks'''
* '''improves''' '''quality''' for '''simple tasks''', but '''worsens''' it for '''complex tasks'''

=== [[Coactor]] ===

Presence of '''peers performing the same task'''

* '''Significantly improves speed''' for performing '''simple tasks''', more than a simple non-expert audience;
* seems to have '''no impact''' on the '''speed''' when performing '''complex tasks''' or '''quality''' when performing '''simple tasks'''
* has '''less but always negative impact''' for the '''quality''' of performing complex tasks;

<ref>{{#cite:Q3901}}</ref>
